title: Campaign Attribution Lab
subtitle: Follow simulated ad displays across the U.S. to five Grand Junction visitor areas.
metaDescription: Watch a Grand Junction campaign, explore individual stops on five street maps and open the verification lab to inspect signed evidence.
imageAlt: Illustrative landscape for a generic fictional campaign example
problem: An advertiser wants to know how many devices with a confirmed ad view later appeared in the destination. One device can appear at several places, and an agency can claim more visits than the evidence supports.
task: Show how an independent verifier could match signed evidence privately and publish an auditable total for the whole region.
actions: Modeled receiving apps that sign view measurements and participating destination gateways that sign local presence observations.
Matched authorized device tokens within one campaign and credited each qualifying device once across the region within 30 days of an app-confirmed view.
Published signed aggregate batches linked by hashes, then let the reader test an agency claim against the private receipts.
results: The Grand Junction map illustrates 10,000 phones shown an ad and 800 later visits, with one stop per visiting phone.
In the regional verification exercise, six signed app views and eight regional observations support two unique matched devices.
A device observed at three regional stops earns one credit. Readers can inspect the excluded examples and verify the downloadable aggregate proof.
notes: The mapped campaign uses simulated visits. The separate regional lab generates evidence locally and exports aggregate counts, signatures and batch commitments. Its device tokens and observations stay in session memory. The receipt and correction exercise is also available from the verification lab.
